mappings.rationale: Composite safeguard requirement for exempted cross-border transfers: DCH-25 governs the restriction of regulated data transfers to third countries generally, PRI-01.5 is the binding-corporate/common-rules instrument (clause B), PRI-07.1 is the mechanism for embedding data-protection clauses in contracts with recipients (clause A, standard contractual clauses), and TPM-05.8 approximates clause C by obtaining independent third-party assessor attestation of a recipient's conformity.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Clause C, 'certificate of accreditation' — SCF has no control for relying on a privacy certification issued by an accredited certification body; TPM-05.8 (independent 3PAO attestation) is the nearest mechanism and is only a partial substitute.

mappings.rationale: The obligation is to embed standard personal-data protection provisions into the inter-body agreement or MoU that authorises the transfer: PRI-07.1 and TPM-05 are the mechanisms for writing data-protection and compliance requirements into agreements with the receiving party, and DCH-25 governs the cross-border transfer itself; confidence is medium because both contract controls are framed around contractor/supplier agreements rather than public-body memoranda of understanding.

This is an applicability clause extending the Law to onward transfers by an offshore recipient; operationally it is discharged by DCH-25 continuing to govern data leaving the Kingdom and by TPM-05.2 flowing the same protection requirements down to the recipient's sub-processors and onward recipients, so the mapping is partial by nature — a scoping provision has no single discrete control.

Direction of obligation: the actor throughout is the competent authority, which may amend the adequacy list and may engage foreign authorities about a country's removal. No duty attaches to a controller or processor, so no SCF control applies.

Direction of obligation: a supervisory power reserved to the competent authority to suspend transfers to a listed country or organisation. The clause imposes nothing on the assessed organisation - any downstream duty to halt a transfer would arise from the suspension decision, not from this text.
Direction of obligation: the competent authority shall issue guides and guidelines. A rule-making duty on the regulator, with no organisational control behind it.
Commencement provision - the Regulation enters into force on publication. Legal boilerplate, not a control requirement of any actor.
